routes.title: Agent Templates - Port Daddy
routes.description: Use the current Port Daddy agent templates: starter fleet YAML, always-on agents, CI repair loops, event-driven ops, remote harbors, research swarms, and secure messaging primitives.

routes.title: Agent Roster - Port Daddy
routes.description: Meet the Port Daddy agent roles that monitor health, salvage crashed work, document drift, coordinate projects, and inspect dependencies.

routes.title: Backend Readiness Is Dependency Truth - Port Daddy
routes.description: A model backend is ready only when credentials, packages, CLI auth, model catalog, and telemetry policy all agree.

routes.title: Bond Pricing Is a Market, Not a Constant - Port Daddy
routes.description: Daily budgets are training wheels. The v2 of the Bonded Commons paper points at the destination: cleanup-cost lower bounds, scope multipliers, the Bonded Advisor pattern, and Thomas Youle's competitive-insurance market.

routes.title: The Control Plane Is the Product - Port Daddy
routes.description: A local agent system is only trustworthy when project identity, file ownership, runtime provenance, backend readiness, cost, and recovery share one inspectable control plane.

routes.title: Coordination Guard Turns Claims Into Policy - Port Daddy
routes.description: Notes and file claims are useful as shared facts. Coordination Guard makes them matter at commit time.

routes.title: Evidence That Survives Multiple Machines - Port Daddy
routes.description: A note that only your laptop can verify is half a record. The v2 Merkle forest, the KMS witness, and the new mutable-signal ledger turn evidence into something a CI pipeline or a teammate can verify in 700 bytes.

routes.title: Cold Start Without Surprise Launches - Port Daddy
routes.description: A good first-run flow should inspect the repo, expose missing credentials, simulate the fleet, and keep the human in control before any agent starts spending money.

routes.title: Passkey Identity Across Machines - Port Daddy
routes.description: Single-node scope was a true description that stopped being true. The Federated Sovereign replaces it with passkey-first identity, an abstract KMS, mobile-as-viewer, and an honest recovery story.

routes.title: PD Tube Turns UI Events Into Agent Work - Port Daddy
routes.description: PD Tube is the small event-reply loop underneath button-to-agent examples, test reporters, editor lightbulbs, and webhook adapters.

routes.title: Keeping the Map Honest - Port Daddy
routes.description: Roadmaps, recovery docs, session notes, and live daemon state drift unless one surface reconciles them into an operator-readable map.

routes.title: Running Is Not the Same as Current - Port Daddy
routes.description: A daemon can be alive, reachable, and still serving the wrong checkout. Runtime provenance has to be visible before you trust UI or CLI behavior.

routes.title: Telemetry Is a Launch Gate - Port Daddy
routes.description: Operator-facing launches should not succeed unless the backend can prove exact tokens, exact rates, and persisted nonzero cost.

routes.title: Blog - Port Daddy
routes.description: Read current Port Daddy field notes about FleetBar, Fleet Control Center, launch readiness, recovery maps, PD Tube, daemon provenance, and coordination policy.

routes.title: API Reference - Port Daddy
routes.description: Inspect Port Daddy API routes, request shapes, response contracts, and the workflows they support.

routes.title: Best Practices - Port Daddy
routes.description: Keep agent work visible, avoid collisions, recover interrupted runs, and promote changes safely.
